section_summary.extract_value: This Results section reports analyses on a single sample (N=84) using bootstrapped mediation models. Across three models, body image flexibility partially mediated the relationships between three types of body size discrepancy (current–personal ideal, current–cultural ideal, current–typical female peer) and body appreciation, and these indirect effects remained significant when controlling for BMI. The section references Table 1 and Fig. 1 Panels A–C for descriptive statistics and graphical representations; no separate studies (e.g., 'Study 1') or multiple sample subsets are indicated.
section_summary.evidence_source: Note: N=84. Table 1 presents the means, standard deviations and the correlational matrix for the primary study variables. In accordance with predictions, across all models tested, body image flexibility was shown to partially mediate the associations between each type of body size discrepancy metric of body dissatisfaction and body appreciation scores.

section_summary.extract_value: Results are reported for a single study (N = 84). Correlations and mediation analyses (bootstrapped with 10,000 resamples) indicate that body image flexibility partially mediated the relationship between three body size discrepancy measures and body appreciation; key indirect effects (e.g., current–personal ideal → body appreciation via flexibility) were statistically significant and remained so when controlling for BMI.
